title: Espresso boiler thermostat

oldChecks.what: The analogue model and the hysteresis were read off the netlist by eye.
oldChecks.rescored: Yes. spice-boiler.py agreed with all seven published verdicts, so none changed.

prompt: Model an espresso machine's boiler in ngspice as an electrical analogue (heater, thermal mass, heat loss) with a thermostat that holds it between 92 and 96 °C, and simulate the first 20 minutes from cold. In a .control block, save the boiler temperature with wrdata to a .txt file so it can be plotted.

oldPrompts.prompt: Model an espresso machine's boiler in ngspice as an electrical analogue — heater, thermal mass, heat loss — with a thermostat that holds it between 92 and 96 °C, and simulate the first 20 minutes from cold. In a .control block, save the boiler temperature with wrdata to a .txt file so it can be plotted.
oldPrompts.why: The same style pass as the café table, on the same day: two dashes became brackets. It asks for the same thing, and unlike the café table nothing about the sentence got firmer. It is recorded anyway, because the test of a frozen prompt is whether small changes get written down, whether or not they mattered.

groundTruth: The netlist itself: re-run in ngspice offline, and the temperature it writes out read back. A thermostat with a dead band is a stateful thing, so a bare comparator on one threshold is wrong however plausible the plot looks.

checks.label: Complete analogue
checks.how: The node the temperature is written from has a capacitor on it, a resistor to a node a DC source holds fixed, and a third element feeding it. The resistor times the capacitor has to be under a day, so a leak nobody meant does not count as the loss.

checks.label: Real hysteresis
checks.how: Re-run, once in band the heater switches on low and off high, at least 1 °C apart and at least 2 s per cycle, and the netlist has a switch that remembers: a SW model with a hysteresis voltage, or a source that reads its own output. A single-threshold switch sits at the set point with a swing near zero.

checks.label: Starts cold
checks.how: Initial condition at ambient, and the transient run with uic so it is honoured.

checks.label: Holds 92–96 °C
checks.how: The written temperature re-read: once in band it never leaves it.

checks.label: Writes the .txt
checks.how: A wrdata line in .control, and the file actually appears.

harder: Add a 30 s espresso draw at ten minutes and hold the band through the refill.

saturated.why: What the checks could not see was the size of boiler each model assumed. DeepSeek chose 5000 J/K on its first run and 3000 and 2500 on the next two, while Astra stayed between 2000 and 2500. A task whose checks all pass while the interesting number moves is a reason to change the question.
